title: AI-Powered Behavior Recognition for Developmental Disability
summary: SK Telecom reports recording time falling from three hours to five minutes and 76.5% fewer self-harm incidents. Its supplied reference does not identify the claimed intervention study.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: SK Telecom reports recording time falling from three hours to five minutes and 76.5% fewer self-harm incidents in a 2024 intervention study. Its supplied reference does not identify that study. The clinical result remains unverified, and AI’s effect is not separated from the other elements of care.
purpose: Help care teams identify and respond to challenging behaviors.

ratings.reason: The source reports that behavior-recording work fell from about three hours to five minutes per session, an aggregate time-saving claim.

SK Telecom reports 76.5% fewer self-harm incidents in a 2024 intervention study, but its supplied reference does not identify that study. Injury severity, duration of the improvement, and AI’s separate effect remain unknown.

ai_role.statement: Vision AI detects and summarizes behavior to support care planning. The submitter reports a reduction in self-harm after an intervention, but the supplied reference does not identify that study and AI's separate contribution is unknown.

evidence.citation: Project account in International Telecommunication Union, AI for Good: Innovate for Impact, 2025. Information current as of June 2025. Outcomes are reported by the project team. The account provides no independent outcome evaluation.
evidence.title: Use Case 5: AI-Powered Behavior Recognition for Developmental Disability

produced_by: Conditions that could produce the benefit are unspecified.

headline: CareVia reports less recording work and self-harm
claim_basis: Sources: the makers' report. The cited evidence includes no independent source and no finding by a regulator or court.
